chunks: First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
The blood money (diyah) of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian is eight hundred dirhams.

Second: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Ibrahim claims that the blood money of the Christian, the Jew, and the Magian is equal. He said: Yes, he speaks the truth.

Third: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub and Ibn Bukayr, from Layth al-Muradi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the blood money of the Christian, the Jew, and the Magian. He said: Their blood money is all equal, eight hundred dirhams, eight hundred dirhams.

Fourth: Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to Bahrain, and he found the blood money of a people from the Jews, Christians, and Magians there. He wrote to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: I found the blood money of a people from the Jews and Christians, and their compensation is eight hundred, eight hundred. And I found the blood money of the Magians, and you had not appointed for me regarding them. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wrote to him saying: Their blood money is like the blood money of the Jews and Christians, and he said: Indeed, they are the People of the Book.

Fifth: Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Durust, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the blood money of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian. He said: They are equal, eight hundred dirhams, eight hundred dirhams.
Sixth: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What is the blood money of the Dhimmi? He said: Eight hundred dirhams.

Seventh: Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Layth al-Muradi and Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The blood money of the Christian and the Jew is eight hundred dirhams.

As for what Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated from Ibn al-Mughira, from Mansur, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The blood money of the Christian, the Jew, and the Magian is the blood money of the Muslim.

And what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever was given a covenant (dhimmah) by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), his blood money is complete. Zurarah said: These [people]. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: And these are among those who were given a covenant.

key_terms.دِرْهَم: A silver coin used as currency
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for killing/injury
key_terms.ذِمَّة: Covenant of protection granted to non-Muslims

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) of Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: These narrations from *Al-Istibsar* clarify the *diyah* (blood money) for *Ahl al-Kitab* (People of the Book) and Zoroastrians, establishing a standard rate of 800 dirhams which is uniform across these groups. While the majority view holds this amount is distinct from the full *diyah* of a Muslim, the tradition of Ibn al-Mughira and Zurarah highlights a scholarly nuance: those granted a specific covenant (*dhimmah*) by the Prophet or Imam may receive complete blood money, reflecting the legal principle that contractual status influences financial compensation. This distinction underscores the Shia juristic approach to balancing general legal rulings with specific historical covenants.
